besluite.rede: 'Teenoor mekaar' means facing each other, whereas the original says the two struts turn against each other at the joint; the preposition swap moves the meaning, the sentence is unchanged since this was dropped before, and the wording matches the finished video.
The generic definite article in 'wat die kragdrade hoog bo die grond oor die land dra' is natural Afrikaans for the wires a pylon carries, so dropping it is a lateral move.

'Vou' is an acceptable Afrikaans way to say a joint folds or gives way (bene vou onder hom in) and fits the lesson's turning-at-joints picture, while 'knak' also carries a snapping or breaking sense, so the claim would shift towards muscles keeping a joint from breaking.
